[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This CoreSite cluster spans Fairfax County and Reston, Virginia, part of the Northern Virginia data center corridor. Wikipedia coverage states that in August 2016 CoreSite purchased the 22 acre Sunrise Technology Park in Reston for 60 million dollars, under then newly appointed CEO Paul Szurek, who replaced retiring CEO Tom Ray in July 2016. Northern Virginia is listed among CoreSite key operating markets as of June 2022. CoreSite was founded in 2001 as CRG West, rebranded to CoreSite in 2009, went public in 2010, and was acquired by American Tower in December 2021. This specific building, VA2, sits on the same Sunrise Technology Park campus as VA1 (12100 Sunrise Valley Drive, also in this registry). CoreSites own Northern Virginia regional page and a separate dedicated operator spec sheet page (both tier-1 operator sources) agree this buildings address is 12098 Sunrise Valley Drive, Reston, VA 20191, with 192,000 plus square feet per the regional page. The same campus includes a third building, VA3, at 12369 Sunrise Valley Drive, 244,000 plus square feet, carrying NVIDIA DGX-Ready certification per the operators own site, VA3 is not itself a row in this registry. No MW or power capacity figure was found for VA2 in any source checked this session.

reading.body:
CoreSite Reston Campus VA2 is a 192,000-square-foot facility in Northern Virginia, a major data center corridor, but the operator has not published its power capacity or IT load specifications. Without these figures, the campus cannot be assessed against the compute-downstream model this site uses to rank AI infrastructure, and thus cannot be evaluated for its role in AI scaling.

The facility sits in Virginia, which has 326 mapped data center facilities but only 23 with published megawatt figures totaling 1,375 MW. CoreSite VA2 ranks 24th by published MW in the state, meaning at least one facility with a published figure exceeds it, but this ranking is uninformative because the campus itself contributes no published number to that total. The absence of a power figure for a 192,000-square-foot CoreSite building in a tier-1 operator market suggests either that capacity is not allocated to this building in isolation, or that CoreSite has chosen not to disclose it.

Until CoreSite publishes power capacity or power density for VA2, this campus remains unmappable to AI workloads and therefore immaterial to tracking whether the grid is the binding constraint on AI scaling in Northern Virginia or elsewhere.
